import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

Reading the lead's report and the diagram manifest done; now checking a prior published report for conventions before restructuring.

Restructuring the lead's report into the canonical file now (bottom line first, unnumbered headings, one proposed diagram to place).

Draft assembled; now fixing a positional "below" reference that moved, reflowing long lines, then validating.

Now validating: content parity with the lead, the diagram fence byte-match, anchors via pandoc, and fence/figure counts.

Validation passes (17 in-doc links resolve, 1 figure div, 2 mermaid fences = lead's 1 + 1 proposed, no external URLs). Writing the canonical file and registering it.

I've published the lead's report as `202611/bank_walk_family_b/bank_walk_family_b.md` in the research repo and registered it as `research:202611/bank_walk_family_b/bank_walk_family_b.md` (ref `file:explicit:fc0cd72b6a22725dfde7de84`). The host will commit it to the research repo after this turn ends.

**Inputs:** there was exactly one source, `research:202611/bank_walk_family_b/bank_walk_family_b__final.md`. The image agent's diagram status was `ready`, with one manifest entry whose source matches the lead's label. I didn't modify the lead's report, the drafts, or the diagram manifest.

**Layout of the new file:**
- It opens in the required order: title, research query, infographic (`bank_walk_family_b_infographic.png`, confirmed present), then `## Bottom line`.
- Sections follow the order a reader's questions come in: Bottom line (the lead's Verdict), Requirement adjustments, Unanimous findings, Recommended design, Architecture, Implementation plan, Conflicts between the reports and how the lead resolved them, Open questions for Bryan, Provenance.
- The lead's opening paragraph about its inputs moved into Provenance.

**Edits to the lead's wording:**
- **Numbered headings removed.** Each of the 10 conflict sections now has a short heading, and its first line carries the lead's original question-and-answer heading in bold as "**Ruling N. …**". That keeps the lead's own "ruling 7" reference meaningful; it now links to that section.
- **Code out of a heading.** "The `b` walker-footer panel" became "The bank walker-footer panel", with `b` moved into the section's first line.
- **Requirement adjustments.** The heading's "(explicit, consolidated)" became a one-line lead-in to the table.
- **Moved reference.** In Provenance, "the ruling below" became a linked "ruling above", because that section now comes before it.
- **Links added:** 17 in-document links, all resolved against the pandoc HTML output. No other wording changed.

**Diagrams:**
- **Accepted:** `landing-retry`, placed under the `figure-landing-retry` anchor right after the Landing paragraph, which contains its anchor text. The fence matches the manifest byte for byte, the caption sits inside the figure block, and one reference sentence links to it.
- **Omitted:** none.
- The lead's own Mermaid diagram and its routing image are unchanged, so the file has 2 Mermaid fences (the lead's 1 plus 1 accepted).

**Links:** the lead's report has no external URLs, so nothing needed checking with curl and nothing was unrepairable. Both relative images, the infographic and `bank_walk_family_b__final_routing.svg`, exist in the report directory.

**Content check:** I compared the new file word by word against the lead's report. Every table row, number, code reference, caveat and open question survived; the only differences are the heading and link edits listed above.

I didn't embed the lead's footer mockup PNG (`bank_row_bracket_walk__cld_footer_mockup.png`). The lead only names it in Provenance, so it stays a text reference there.
